openQuestions.question: Datum's hold says only that the cell rides trams and sky rail between stops and stations. Is riding a fast-travel power at all? If so, does it cost anything (cash, Trail, Alert, cooldown) and where can the player board?
openQuestions.why: The GDD sets no power, price, fare or rule for riding as fast travel, so none is written into the timetable.

openQuestions.question: If riding is priced or limited, what are the cost and limits? Does the cell wait for the scheduled vehicle or take an instant hop?
openQuestions.why: Pricing belongs to Motive. Journey times assume a real vehicle and count in-vehicle time only.

openQuestions.question: Do headway and dwell need to match any mission window, e.g. the handover timings?
openQuestions.why: The starting headways and dwells are Pulse's own values and are not drawn from the GDD.

notes: Run time = chainage gap ÷ stated average speed, including accel/braking: tram 10 m/s, sky rail 12 m/s. Starting values [S], tune by playtest.
Headway (tram 120 s, sky rail 90 s) and dwell (tram 15 s, sky rail 12 s) are my starting values; the GDD gives none. Motive and Keel to confirm.
Journey sec = in-vehicle run time plus dwell at intermediate stops only. It excludes waiting, interchange walking and any boarding cost, none of which the GDD sets.
Interchange pairs: T1/records-T2/market, T1/circus-S1/circus, T2/parade-S1/harbour. 'via' names the interchange stop on the line the journey leaves; [] means no interchange.
Journeys that start at an interchange stop are listed from the other line's stop so that every second counted is a ride (e.g. T1/comet to T2/sunset = 31 + 43.1 = 74.1).

T1 and T2 are through-running, with termini off-sheet. The T1 circus loop and S1 skyport loop have no stop ids, so they are not timed. The earlier skyport runs were removed because no such stop exists.
Reverse runs are assumed symmetric. Only stops on the sheet are timetabled.
